title: The Marquis of Mirabel to Carlos Coloma, Lyon, 8 December 1622 (BNE RES/227/122): key partial by our protocol, read in part

documents.route: Antonio Dávila y Zúñiga, Marquis of Mirabel, Spanish ambassador in France -> Carlos Coloma, Spanish ambassador in London

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the letter; the key comes from the margin clears of the Duke of Feria's letters to Coloma (RES/227/127-129).

transcription.source: BNE Digital (CC BY 4.0; one crop on the site write-up)
transcription.notes: Re-read on the image twice; 16 places settled by a blind shape sheet answered by Brice Dudout (5 Nov), then two more blind sheets (FL2-C, 15 questions; FS1, 6 questions; 11 Nov): four signs re-read (1v.05 for, 1v.10 4, 1v.14 88, 1v.18 84). Marked signs (barred 4, q with a stroke below, x with two dots below, and those seen on FL2-C) have no value.

system.summary: Syllabary on a grid (fV = tV, xV = nV, cVr = rV, xVr = sV, sVr = cV, sVn = pV, fVn = pVr, frV = gV, Vs = mV), two-digit numbers for letters and syllables, three-digit numbers and underlined tokens for code words, ligatures faz/fez/fuz = que; marked signs are distinct signs.
system.notes: The same system as the Duke of Feria's letters to Coloma (BNE RES/227/120-129) and BNE MSS/18428 (Mirabel to Gondomar).

prior_solution.where: No decipherment on the letter. No edition found (two web searches); nothing on DECODE, at Cryptiana (Tomokiyo) or in Lasry's lists; catalogue 1601 open, no target, PR or issue on origin/main (GitHub API, 895f21c4, 5 Nov 2026). Not read: M. Á. Guill Ortega, Carlos Coloma (2007); Herrero García (Avisos, 2023) on MSS/18428; the Codoin index.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target, set the rules (protocols and amendments hashed before each computation, one measurement per held-out passage, thresholds fixed in advance) and answered the three blind shape sheets (shapes only; M16, FL2-C, FS1). AI agents transcribed, rebuilt the key, measured, read and wrote up. No palaeographer checked the letter.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout
Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), one text-only run (code-value proposals, 11 Nov 2026)

solution.what: Grid and syllabary deduced from the margin clears of Feria's letters (RES/227/120); key K-C01 frozen and measured once on Mirabel f.1v ll. 12-21 by M5: 0.333 vs 0.169.
CLE_C02 frozen, measured once on RES/227/127 f.1r against its margin clear: 0.761 vs 0.437 (gap 0.324).
CLE_C03 measured once on RES/227/128 f.1v: 0.690 vs 0.419 (gap 0.271); then H4 (MSS/18428 p. 15) burned without measurement (show-through, not a clear).
CLE_C04 measured once on MSS/18428 p. 44 right against its margin clear: 0.814 vs 0.466 (gap 0.348).
Letter read word by word, all 969 tokens covered in order; blind shape sheet of 16 questions applied: 425 words, 338 certain, 37 probable, 29 restored, 21 unresolved (88.2%).

141 = ello and 318 = oficio from the clear copy of MSS/18428 fol. 31; code values proposed by sense and the alphabetical order of the nomenclator (text-only Claude Fable 5.2 run); blind shape sheets FL2-C (controls 2/2) and FS1 (controls 2/2, 4 of 4 conjectures confirmed; position bias declared, answers confirmed by shape by Brice Dudout). No new key measurement. 421 words: 337 certain, 47 probable, 31 restored, 6 unresolved (91.2%). See BLIND-REREADING.md.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from the contemporary margin clears of other letters in the same system (the Duke of Feria to Coloma, RES/227/120-129), then applied to Mirabel's letter, which has no decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (certain + probable; restored not counted), counted by script on the word table of reading.md, which covers the transcription in order: 421 words, 337 certain, 47 probable, 31 restored, 6 unresolved = 384/421 = 91.2% (11 Nov 2026; 88.2% on 5 Nov). Stricter count (M16 pre-registration for the xe words, two-place proposals restored): 378/421 = 89.8%.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py), characters against contemporary clears, thresholds >= 0.85 and >= +0.30: C02 0.761 vs 0.437 (partial), H3 0.690 vs 0.419 (failed), H5 0.814 vs 0.466 (partial); C01 (M5, no clear) 0.333 vs 0.169 (failed); H4 burned without measurement (show-through).

credits.note: transcription, key rebuilt from Feria's margin clears and tested on held-out clears (partial by our protocol), letter read in part (88.2% on 5 Nov, 91.2% on 11 Nov after three blind shape sheets), translation
the margin clears of the Duke of Feria's letters to Coloma (RES/227/127-129) and of MSS/18428 p. 44, used to build and test the key; the clear copy of MSS/18428 fol. 31 (141 = ello, 318 = oficio)
catalogue entry 1601 and leads 1602 (Feria) and 1271 (Mirabel to Gondomar)

gaps.item: 6 unresolved words: code 39 (two places), bo, code 2, [ge]ia, z cer zan
Marked signs 4‡, q̲, x̤ and those seen on FL2-C (no value); 31 restored words, among them the code values at one place (127, 40, 264, 295, 35, 53, K, 68, 81, 139, 317, R, 62, L/54/y)
gaps.detail: a new letter of the system with a contemporary clear is needed

texts.label: RES/227/122, f.1r-f.1v: cipher body of the letter
texts.summary: Louis XIII's proposals to the Duke of Savoy (Valtellina, help in case of rupture, Geneva), the French answer and the Duke's return from Avignon; Mirabel's talk with the Queen Mother on the deposit of the Valtellina forts, a Lorraine garrison and the capitulations of Aranjuez, the Catholic religion to be kept there; Richelieu, not of the King's Council, governs the Queen Mother.

reading_review.note: Read again as sentences 11 Nov 2026 by one AI reader after the blind sheets FL2-C and FS1 (Brice Dudout answered the shape sheets only; FS1 position bias declared, answers confirmed by shape). The letter construes as Spanish sentences throughout, with gaps: 337 certain, 47 probable, 31 restored, 6 unresolved of 421 words (91.2%), so read in part. Most new code values are machine proposals by sense and key order (restored at one place).

outcome.notes: New key for the Mirabel/Feria cipher of 1622 (key.tsv, CC BY 4.0), partial by our protocol.
